findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body: When tenants share the database, `getDocument` still receives `ctx.tenantId`, but the changed call and query discard it and filter only by `documentId`. Overlapping or attacker-supplied IDs can therefore return another tenant’s record, creating a cross-tenant disclosure regression.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body: Deleting `src/cache.ts` removes the exported `readCached` module. Existing consumers importing this path will fail module resolution, contrary to the stated goal of preserving existing contracts. Retain the module or provide a compatible replacement.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body:
When two tenants have the same `documentId`, the query now matches both tenants’ records. Depending on `db.find` semantics and record ordering, `getDocument` can return another tenant’s document or an ambiguous result; concurrent inserts can change which record wins.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
`getDocument` still receives a tenant-bearing context, but the query now filters only by `documentId`. In a multi-tenant database, a caller who supplies another tenant’s document ID can retrieve that document, or duplicate IDs can resolve to the wrong tenant.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` removes the exported `readCached` API. Any downstream TypeScript code importing this module will fail module resolution/compilation after upgrading, contrary to the stated contract-preservation goal.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
When multiple tenants share `ctx.db`, an authenticated caller who supplies another tenant’s document ID can retrieve that document because the query no longer constrains `tenantId`. This introduces a cross-tenant data disclosure/IDOR regression.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
